title: Dialect-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Arabic Question Answering: Measuring and Mitigating the Moroccan Darija–MSA Retrieval Gap
content: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems for Arabic are evaluated almost exclusively with Modern Standard Arabic (MSA) queries, although users write in dialect. We study this mismatch with a parallel benchmark of 200 questions written in both MSA and Moroccan Darija over 3,054 Arabic Wikipedia passages. Dialectal queries lower hybrid-retrieval Recall@1 from 0.755 to 0.620, and the loss reaches the answers: with five retrieved passages, answer correctness falls from 0.810 to 0.690, mostly through additional refusals; part of this loss persists even when the gold passage is supplied directly, so retrieval is the larger but not the only component. Rewriting Darija queries into MSA does not help. Zero-shot cross-encoder reranking raises dialectal Recall@1 to 0.800 (MSA: 0.755 unreranked, 0.875 reranked) and lets a single retrieved passage replace five unreranked passages with no loss larger than five percentage points and a 3.7-fold shorter prompt. Because dialectal queries are retrieved with lower confidence, gating the reranker on the retriever’s score margin concentrates its cost on them without any dialect detection, retaining 94% of the benefit while reranking about half of the queries. The findings hold under a human-validated LLM judge (Cohen’s κ=0.797), Holm correction and three prompt wordings, and replicate judge-free on a second, Darija-trained generator. We release the benchmark, corpus, code and all result files.
